questions.question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct? 

5 and 4

I. 4 + 8 × 5 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

II. 5 × 3 - 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1a2f9ab33e780cba5010b6de702b28619de1d1b1c922808fce2123379d05d37.png] 

I. Given equation : 4 + 8 × 5 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

After interchanging the given two numbers 5 and 4 the equation is as follows : 5 + 8 × 4 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

⇒ 5 + 8 × 4 - __**7 ÷ 1**__ = 30

⇒ 5 + __**8 × 4**__ - 7 = 30

⇒ __**5 + 32**__ - 7 = 30

⇒ __**37 - 7**__ = 30

⇒ **30 = 30**

**LHS = RHS**

II. Given equation : 5 × 3 - 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11

After interchanging the given two numbers 5 and 4 the equation is as follows : 4 × 3 - 5 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11

⇒ 4 × 3 - 5 + __**6 ÷ 2**__ = 11

⇒ __**4 × 3**__ - 5 + 3 = 11

⇒ __**12**__ - 5 __**+ 3**__ = 11

⇒ __**15 - 5**__ = 11

⇒ 10 ≠ 11

LHS ≠ RHS

∴ Here, only equation I is true.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only I".**

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All bike are cycle.

II. Some cycle are tub.

**Conclusion:**

I. All tub are bike.

II. All cycle are tub.

III. All cycle are bike.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28034bf34340a7a6ef4906521bed9fd242e34fb93ed38d045c78fafe61fff99d.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c29591e6b53667cd6eeaacbc3cc14fef57b7892002f813c0d57b8cf2f6a66c5.png] 

Conclusion:

I. All tub are bike → False (Some cycle are tub and All bike are cycle so, All tub are bike is false)

II. All cycle are tub → False (Some cycle are tub so, All cycle are tub is false)

III. All cycle are bike → False (All bike are cycle so, All cycle are bike is false)

Hence, the correct answer is **"Neither conclusion follows".**

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship in set as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 

(64, 8, 16)

(40, 20, 4)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **First number = (Second number × Third number) ÷ 2**

**(64, 8, 16)** → (8 × 16) ÷ 2 → 128 ÷ 2 = 64

**(40, 20, 4)** → (20 × 4) ÷ 2 → 80 ÷ 2 = 40

Let's check each option as per the logic,

**1) (56, 14, 8) → (14 × 8) ÷ 2 → 112 ÷ 2 = 56**

2) (100, 50, 8) → (50 × 8) ÷ 2 → 400 ÷ 2 ≠ 100

3) (120, 100, 5) → (100 × 5) ÷ 2 → 500 ÷ 2 ≠ 120

4) (54, 9, 14) → (9 × 14) ÷ 2 → 126 ÷ 2 ≠ 54

Here, we can see that only option 1 follow the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"(56, 14, 8)".**

questions.question: Weight of five pens P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5 is compared. Weight of P3 is less than P1 but more than P2, Weight of P2 is more than only two pens. Weight of P5 is not the least. If the weight of P5 is 100 grams, then what can be the weight of P1?
questions.solution:
Weight of five pens P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5 is compared.

1) Weight of P3 is less than P1 but more than P2.

P1 > P3 > P2.

2) Weight of P2 is more than only two pens and Weight of P5 is not the least.

P1 > P3 > P2 > P5 > P4

∴ If the weight of P5 is 100 grams, then the weight of P1 should be more than 100 grams.

Here in option only '108' is more than 100 grams.

Hence, the correct answer is **"108".**

questions.question:
By Interchanging which two signs the equation will be correct? 

27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

By using BODMAS RULE:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

**Option 1****):**** **+ and -

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 ÷ 3 + 18 - 3 × 2 = 18

⇒ __**27 ÷ 3**__ + 18 - 3 × 2 = 18

⇒ 9 + 18 - __**3 × 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**9 + 18**__ - 6 = 18

⇒ __**27 - 6 **__= 18

⇒ 21 ≠ 18

LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 2****):**** × and +**

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 × 3 + 2 = 18

⇒ __**27 ÷ 3**__ - 18 × 3 + 2 = 18

⇒ 9 - __**18 × 3**__ + 2 = 18

⇒ __**9**__ - 54 __**+ 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**11 **____**- 54**__ = 18

⇒ - 43 ≠ 18

LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 3****):**** + and ÷ **

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 + 3 - 18 ÷ 3 × 2 = 18

⇒ 27 + 3 - __**18 ÷ 3**__ × 2 = 18

⇒ 27 + 3 - __**6 × 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**27 + 3**__ - 12 = 18

⇒ __**30 - 12**__ = 18

⇒ **18 = 18**

**LHS = RHS**

**Option 4****):**** ÷ and × **

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 × 3 - 18 + 3 ÷ 2 = 18

⇒ 27 × 3 - 18 + __**3 ÷ 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**27 × 3**__ - 18 + 1.5 = 18

⇒ __**81**__ - 18 __**+ 1.5**__ = 18

⇒ 82.5 - 18 = 18

⇒ 64.5 ≠ 18

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"+ and ÷".**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

67 : 336 :: 43 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Second number = (First number × 5) + 1**

**67: 336** → (67 × 5) + 1 → 335 + 1 = 336

**43:**** ? → (43 × 5) + 1 → 215 + 1 = 216**

Hence, the correct answer is **"216".**
